Building 2.5D parallax multi-plane camera systems: converting 2D layers into 3D, positioning layers in Z-depth, adding a 35mm virtual camera and two-node null controller, enabling Depth of Field, and animating smooth camera fly-throughs. Structuring reusable pre-comps, saving animation presets (.ffx), configuring realistic motion blur, and implementing render and preview optimization.
subtopics: Brand motion rules: codifying duration tokens, easing curves, and transition choreography for animation continuity
2.5D parallax architecture: positioning 2D graphic and photographic layers across 3D Z-depth space
Camera rigging: creating two-node camera rigs with master controller nulls, Depth of Field, and aperture blur
Reusable pre-comps and template structure: engineering modular composition hierarchies that update globally
Animation presets: creating and saving custom .ffx presets for rapid one-click deployment
Motion blur and render and preview optimization: multi-frame rendering setup, memory allocation, and disk cache clearing
lessons.why_it_matters: Enterprise clients require cohesive motion systems across all brand assets; 2.5D parallax elevates flat 2D designs into cinematic dimensional experiences.
lessons.what_learner_does: Builds a 2.5D parallax camera scene with motion blur, establishes brand motion rules for animation continuity, and creates reusable pre-comps and animation presets.
lessons.expected_outcome: A 2.5D parallax camera fly-through sequence and a documented brand motion design system with reusable animation presets.

Parallax and depth distribution: positioning layers in Z-space to achieve natural depth separation during camera moves
Depth of field configuration: animating Focus Distance, Aperture, and Blur Level for cinematic shallow focus
AI-generated plate integration: matching horizon lines, vanishing points, and lens distortion of AI background plates
Perspective matching: aligning virtual camera coordinates to physical plate geometry
lessons.why_it_matters: 2.5D environments allow editors and motion designers to create sweeping cinematic camera moves through static artwork and matte paintings.
lessons.what_learner_does: Constructs a multi-plane 2.5D environment using camera layers, integrates an AI-generated matte painting plate with perspective matching, and animates a cinematic camera move with depth of field.

lessons.lesson_title: Lighting, Shadows, Atmospheric Effects & Compositing Realism
lessons.what_is_taught: Lighting simulation in composite scenes: setting key lights, fill lights, ambient lights, and inverse-square falloff curves. Shadows engineering: configuring Cast Shadows, Shadow Darkness, and Shadow Diffusion to ground synthetic objects onto physical floors. Surface reflections: building environmental floor and table reflections using blurred inverted duplicate layers with opacity falloff. Atmospheric effects and particles: introducing volumetric fog, light rays, dust motes, and particle systems to create atmospheric perspective. Scene interaction and scene continuity: ensuring light direction, color temperature, and contrast match across sequential shots. Compositing realism audits: eliminating floating elements, synthetic black-point mismatches, and unreal edge sharpness.
subtopics: Lighting simulation: directional key lights, fill lights, ambient lights, and inverse-square falloff
Shadows engineering: configuring Cast Shadows, Shadow Darkness, and Shadow Diffusion for contact grounding
Reflections: building ground and table reflections using blurred inverted duplicate layers with falloff
Atmospheric effects and particles: adding subtle dust motes, floating embers, volumetric light rays, and smoke
Scene interaction: simulating light spill and color bounce between composite layers and live-action elements
Compositing realism and scene continuity: auditing light angles, black levels, and optical characteristics across sequential shots
lessons.why_it_matters: Shadows, reflections, and atmospheric particles provide the essential subconscious cues that convince the human eye a composite scene is physically real.
lessons.what_learner_does: Adds realistic directional lighting, contact shadows, floor reflections, and atmospheric particles to a synthetic element, auditing compositing realism.
lessons.expected_outcome: A photorealistic commercial VFX composition with grounded shadows, convincing reflections, atmospheric particles, and perfect scene continuity.
lessons.example: Compositing a synthetic sports car onto a live-action asphalt road with realistic tire contact shadows, headlights casting volumetric fog, and wet road reflections.

modules.module_purpose: Master professional color science and grading in DaVinci Resolve: Resolve interface, Cut/Edit/Color workflows, primary colour correction (exposure, white balance, contrast), video scopes (waveform, RGB parade, vectorscope, histogram), node-based grading, shot matching, skin-tone correction, Power Windows, qualifiers, tracking, Rec.709, Log footage, LUTs, color management, colour-space transforms, cinematic looks, brand colour consistency, HDR/SDR awareness, and export colour integrity (with clear demarcation of free tools vs Studio-only neural features like IntelliSearch and CineFocus).

Execute precise shot matching across diverse camera angles and changing lighting conditions.

Free vs Studio Feature Demarcation & Export Colour Integrity

lessons.lesson_title: DaVinci Resolve Interface, Video Scopes & Primary Colour Correction
lessons.what_is_taught: DaVinci Resolve interface navigation: Media, Cut, Edit, Color, and Deliver pages; Cut/Edit/Color workflows. Reading and interpreting video scopes: Waveform (evaluating luminance distribution), RGB Parade (analyzing color balance across red, green, and blue channels), Vectorscope (measuring hue and saturation), and Histogram. Primary colour correction: setting black points with Lift, balancing midtones with Gamma, and shaping peak highlights with Gain. Controlling exposure, white balance, and contrast using primary color wheels, temp/tint sliders, and custom curves. Enforcing broadcast legal signal ranges.
subtopics: Resolve interface navigation: Cut/Edit/Color workflows, media pool management, and viewer transport
Video scopes analysis: Waveform, RGB Parade, Vectorscope, and Histogram calibration
Primary colour correction: Lift, Gamma, Gain, and Offset tonal adjustments
Exposure, white balance, and contrast: neutral grey balancing and tonal curve sculpting
Broadcast legality: monitoring clip levels to prevent crushed blacks (<0 IRE) and blown highlights (>100 IRE)
lessons.why_it_matters: Primary color correction establishes the neutral baseline for all visual storytelling; uncalibrated footage leads to muddy shadows, clipped highlights, and disjointed edits.
lessons.what_learner_does: Calibrates the Resolve interface, reads video scopes, neutralizes color casts, and balances exposure and contrast on a raw multicam scene.
lessons.expected_outcome: A perfectly neutralized, exposure-balanced sequence conforming to broadcast legal limits on waveform and RGB parade scopes.
lessons.example: Correcting a tungsten-cast interior shot so white shirts appear neutral at 128 on the RGB Parade and skin tones fall naturally.

lessons.lesson_title: Node-Based Grading, Log Footage Normalization & Colour-Space Transforms
lessons.what_is_taught: Building robust node-based grading architectures: serial nodes, parallel nodes, layer mixer nodes, and compound node trees. Understanding Log footage: wide dynamic range, logarithmic gamma curves, and desaturated flat profiles (Sony S-Log3, Canon C-Log2, Apple Log). Professional color management: DaVinci YRGB vs DaVinci YRGB Color Managed (RCM) vs ACES. Deploying Colour-space transforms (CST): non-destructively mapping camera raw Log gamuts into standard Rec.709. Utilizing 3D LUTs: technical conversion LUTs vs creative look LUTs, avoiding clipping, and generating custom show LUTs (.cube).
subtopics: Node-based grading architecture: structuring serial, parallel, and layer mixer node pipelines
Log footage characteristics: wide dynamic range capture and flat logarithmic profiles
Color management systems: DaVinci YRGB Color Managed vs ACES color workflows
Colour-space transforms (CST): accurately converting camera Log gamuts into Rec.709 standard
LUTs application: technical normalization LUTs vs creative styling LUTs (.cube)
lessons.why_it_matters: Colour-space transforms preserve maximum dynamic range and color bit-depth far better than destructive one-click LUTs.
lessons.what_learner_does: Constructs a standardized 8-node grading tree, normalizes mixed Log footage using Colour-Space Transforms, and builds custom show LUTs.
lessons.expected_outcome: A standardized node tree template that normalizes multi-camera Log footage into a rich Rec.709 color space without clipped data.
lessons.example: Applying a CST node to convert 10-bit Sony S-Log3 footage into Rec.709, retaining delicate cloud detail in the highlights.

lessons.lesson_title: Secondary Grading: Power Windows, Qualifiers & Skin-Tone Correction
lessons.what_is_taught: Secondary color grading precision: isolating specific colors, saturations, and luminance levels using HSL and 3D Qualifiers. Power Windows: linear, circular, polygon, and curve windows for regional lighting adjustments. High-speed planar tracking in Resolve: locking Power Windows to moving faces, hands, and scene elements. Skin-tone correction: isolating actor skin tones, analyzing alignment along the Vectorscope skin-tone line across diverse ethnicities, and smoothing skin texture. Demarcation of free vs Studio-only Resolve features: understanding IntelliSearch where available and CineFocus where supported versus manual grading tools.

Power Windows: shaping vignettes, spotlights, and regional correction masks
Tracking: planar tracking Power Windows to moving subjects through camera movement
Skin-tone correction: aligning hues along the Vectorscope skin-tone line across diverse ethnicities
Free vs Studio-only Resolve tools: evaluating IntelliSearch where available and CineFocus where supported vs manual grading equivalents
lessons.why_it_matters: Viewers immediately spot unnatural skin tones; secondary qualifiers and Power Windows allow colorists to sculpt lighting and protect human skin tones.
lessons.what_learner_does: Isolates an actor's face with a circular Power Window, tracks it with the planar tracker, qualifies skin tones to align with the skin-tone line, and refines contrast.
lessons.expected_outcome: Flawlessly corrected, natural skin tones that remain locked to the subject across rapid camera movement.
lessons.example: Tracking a Power Window onto an actress walking through changing sunlight to keep her skin tones warm and consistent without altering the background.

lessons.lesson_title: Shot Matching, Cinematic Looks, Brand Colour Consistency & Export Integrity
lessons.what_is_taught: Executing seamless shot matching across an entire sequence: matching exposure, contrast, and color balance between A-cam and B-cam setups. Designing stylized cinematic looks: teal & orange split-toning, filmic warmth, bleach bypass, and analog grain emulation. Enforcing brand colour consistency: locking corporate hex/Pantone colors to ensure brand logos and product colors are not distorted by creative looks. HDR/SDR awareness: understanding high dynamic range color volume (Rec.2020) versus SDR Rec.709 delivery. Export colour integrity: resolving the QuickTime gamma shift bug (gamma 1.96 vs 2.4 vs 2.2), setting color space tags, and conducting final scope QA.
subtopics: Shot matching methodology: matching exposure, black levels, and skin tones across sequential camera angles
Cinematic looks: developing filmic palettes, split-toning, and aesthetic grain textures
Brand colour consistency: isolating and preserving exact corporate brand colors from global look grades
HDR/SDR awareness: color volume considerations, peak brightness limits, and mastering standards
Export colour integrity: calibrating QuickTime gamma tags (Rec.709-A) to ensure colors display identically across web, mobile, and broadcast monitors
lessons.why_it_matters: Inconsistent color between shots distracts viewers, while gamma shifts during export ruin days of grading work; export colour integrity ensures the client sees exactly what you graded.
lessons.what_learner_does: Shot-matches 6 sequential scenes from an interview, crafts an intentional cinematic look, protects brand colors, and renders master files with verified export colour integrity.
lessons.expected_outcome: A fully graded 90-second cinematic scene featuring 6 matched multi-camera shots with consistent skin tones, intentional look, and verified export color tags.
lessons.example: Matching a close-up shot from an iPhone with a wide shot from an ARRI Alexa, applying a film print look, and ensuring the company's trademark cyan logo remains spot-on.

modules.assessment_criteria: Shot-to-shot color balance & exposure consistency (40%), Skin tone naturalism & scope compliance (35%), Cinematic look aesthetic & brand consistency (25%).

lessons.lesson_title: Sound-Effect Layering, Loudness Normalization & Audio Quality Control
lessons.what_is_taught: Crafting rich soundscapes: sound-effect layering with Foley footsteps, clothing rustle, atmospheric room tone, and subtle ambience beds. lessons.lesson_title: Subtitles, Versioning, Project Archiving & Final Render Checklist

Audio/video sync and colour consistency: verifying 2-pop sync markers, audio drift across long timelines, and gamma tag matching (NCLC 1-1-1 tags). lessons.lesson_title: Video Prompt Engineering: Optics, Camera Dynamics & Lighting Syntax
lessons.what_is_taught: Systematic video prompt engineering syntax: defining subject, action, environment, composition, and camera angle. Optical parameters: lens and focal-length concepts (e.g. 24mm wide angle, 50mm natural, 85mm portrait, 35mm anamorphic with subtle horizontal flare). Directing camera movement: pans, tilts, push-ins, tracking dollies, crane booms, and orbital sweeps. Lighting design: golden hour sunlight, chiaroscuro, volumetric haze, soft studio box diffusion, and colour and mood descriptors. Movement direction, timing, continuity, sound and dialogue cues, desired aspect ratio (16:9, 9:16), shot duration (4s, 5s, 8s), and style references.
subtopics: Prompt syntax hierarchy: structuring Subject, Action, Environment, Composition, and Lighting tags
Lens and focal-length concepts: directing optical characteristics (shallow depth of field, anamorphic bokeh, focal length)
Camera movement and movement direction: specifying smooth camera trajectories (dolly-in, tracking, pedestal, roll)
Lighting, colour and mood: controlling color temperature (5600K daylight vs 3200K tungsten), contrast ratios, and atmosphere
Timing and continuity cues: specifying action pacing, duration limits, and sound and dialogue cues
Aspect ratio and style references: formatting prompts for landscape 16:9, vertical 9:16, and cinematic film stock references
lessons.why_it_matters: Precise optical, camera, and lighting terminology produces cinematographic video generations, whereas vague, hype-filled prompts produce chaotic video morphing.
lessons.what_learner_does: Engineers a suite of 6 detailed video prompts adhering to optical, lighting, and movement syntax guidelines across 16:9 and 9:16 aspect ratios.
lessons.expected_outcome: A structured prompt matrix specifying optics, camera movement, lighting, and continuity cues for every shot in the commercial breakdown.
lessons.example: Crafting a prompt specifying an 85mm f/1.4 lens, low-angle push-in camera movement, 1000W rim lighting, and 24fps motion for an athlete portrait.

Interpolation planning: designing starting frame and ending frame keyframes to connect adjacent shots seamlessly and avoid implausible transitions. Formulating an editing plan before generation to identify exact transition points and handles.
subtopics: Character consistency frameworks: utilizing facial reference images, fixed seed values, and immutable wardrobe tokens
Product appearance preservation: protecting trademarked brand contours, logo placement, and materials from AI hallucination
Location continuity: establishing consistent architectural landmarks, weather, and environmental horizons
Camera direction, light direction, and screen direction: mapping key light placement and eye-lines to prevent continuity breaks
Starting frame and ending frame planning: designing matching visual landmarks to connect adjacent shots seamlessly
Avoiding implausible transitions & editing plan before generation: planning cuts, wipes, and match-cuts prior to generation
lessons.why_it_matters: A commercial cannot tell a coherent narrative if the protagonist's face or product packaging morphs noticeably between cuts.
lessons.what_learner_does: Builds a consistency blueprint for a protagonist and product, mapping light direction, screen direction, starting/ending frames, and editing cut points.
lessons.expected_outcome: A documented consistency blueprint defining character tokens, product references, lighting vectors, and an editing plan before generation.

lessons.lesson_title: Quality Control, Artifact Diagnosis & Failure Recovery
lessons.what_is_taught: Systematic quality control for AI video output: frame-by-frame inspection protocols. Diagnosing common generative flaws: temporal flicker, frame consistency anomalies, facial artifacts (warping, melting features), product distortion (hallucinated logos, morphed packaging), incorrect motion direction (backwards motion, floating physics), camera continuity errors, lighting mismatches, inconsistent shadows, text/brand corruption, and unexpected audio. Formulating clip failure recovery strategies: determining when to re-prompt and regenerate versus when to repair manually in After Effects/Premiere (compositing, rotoscoping, clean-plating, speed-ramping, or framing punch-ins).
subtopics: Temporal flicker and frame consistency: identifying frame-to-frame luminance variations and surface boiling
Facial artifacts and product distortion: catching anatomical errors, melting fingers, and distorted brand logos
Motion and camera continuity errors: diagnosing impossible physics, inverted motion direction, and lighting mismatches
Inconsistent shadows and text/brand corruption: auditing cast shadow angles and corrupted on-screen typography
Unexpected audio anomalies: inspecting generated audio tracks and isolating unwanted synthetic artifacts
Clip failure recovery matrix: calculating time/credit costs of regeneration vs manual repair in NLE/compositing suites
lessons.why_it_matters: Commercial clients will immediately reject video containing melting faces or deformed brand logos; rigorous QC and recovery workflows separate amateurs from professional directors.
lessons.what_learner_does: Conducts a rigorous QC audit on 8 generated video clips, documents visual and temporal defects, and performs clip failure recovery via regeneration and manual patching.
lessons.expected_outcome: A documented AI QC inspection report and repaired, artifact-free video sequence ready for timeline assembly.
lessons.example: Catching a frame where a model's hand develops 6 fingers, freezing that frame, and patching it with a clean plate in After Effects.

Project organization: structuring footage bins (01_REAL, 02_AI_GENERATED, 03_VOX, 04_MOGRT) and media caching

Camera/perspective matching & optical grain: aligning vanishing points and adding uniform sensor noise

Content provenance and C2PA: embedding and reading cryptographic metadata to verify media authenticity
AI disclosure standards in advertising: FTC, EU AI Act, and ASCI regulatory compliance in commercial marketing
Consent for synthetic likeness and voice cloning permission: legal model releases and biometric authorization
No impersonation without authorization: strict prohibitions against deepfakes, celebrity clones, and unauthorized voices
Client confidentiality and enterprise data security: configuring opt-outs for training data collection
lessons.why_it_matters: Unlicensed AI generation, unauthorized voice cloning, or failure to disclose synthetic media creates catastrophic copyright and legal liability for agencies and brands.
lessons.what_learner_does: Drafts an AI production compliance package including client disclosure statement, voice cloning release, and C2PA provenance audit.
lessons.expected_outcome: A certified legal and ethical compliance package covering commercial licensing, synthetic likeness consent, and C2PA disclosure.

lessons.lesson_title: Commercial Operational Management: Budgeting, Logs & Handoff
lessons.what_is_taught: Operational management of commercial AI production: managing AI generation credits, tracking GPU compute, and establishing iteration budgeting to prevent massive cost overruns. Maintaining generation logs: recording prompt strings, seed numbers, model versions, reference assets, and parameter settings to ensure reproducible project organization. Clarifying source file ownership: raw generations, layered project files (.prproj, .aep), and final master deliverables. Formulating client handoff requirements: packaging master videos, licensing certificates, prompt documentation, and raw asset archives.
subtopics: AI generation credits and compute budgeting: tracking platform costs per shot and setting generation limits
Generation logs management: logging seeds, prompts, model versions, and settings for 100% reproducibility
Reproducible project organization: directory taxonomy separating raw generations, approved selects, and clean plates
Source file ownership and contractual IP boundaries: establishing what the client owns (deliverable vs prompt IP)
Client handoff requirements: delivering master renders, textless archives, font licenses, and AI generation ledgers
lessons.why_it_matters: Without structured generation logs and iteration budgeting, AI projects become unreproducible money pits where lost seeds make minor revisions impossible.
lessons.what_learner_does: Establishes an iteration budget, tracks generation credits across a 6-shot sequence, maintains a prompt/seed log, and compiles a client handoff archive.
lessons.expected_outcome: A comprehensive project operations ledger featuring generation logs, compute budgets, and a formal client handoff package.
lessons.example: Providing a client with a full CSV generation log linking each 4K video file to its exact prompt, seed, model version, and commercial license.

lessons.lesson_title: Client Brief, Creative Strategy, Storyboard & Animatic
lessons.what_is_taught: Inception phase of an enterprise commercial production: client brief interpretation, decoding commercial objectives, target audience demographics, and calls to action (CTA). Formulating creative strategy and pitch deck. Asset inventory and budget planning: organizing raw footage, graphics, and music licenses. Establishing production schedules, team roles, and creative milestones. Developing detailed visual storyboards and seeking storyboard approval. Building a timed animatic with scratch voiceover and temporary music to lock editorial pacing and sequence duration before executing final motion graphics and VFX.
subtopics: Client brief interpretation: extracting core value propositions, campaign tone, and mandatory brand guidelines
Creative strategy and story concept: developing high-impact narrative hooks and persuasive commercial structures
Production schedule and milestones: establishing deadlines for script lock, animatic sign-off, rough cut, and picture lock
Asset inventory and licensing: cataloging live footage, stock clips, brand vector kits, and audio stems
Storyboard approval: presenting style frames, camera annotations, and visual concepts to simulated client boards
Animatic development: constructing a timed 2D animatic to lock pacing, voiceover cadence, and shot transitions

Cutting traditional footage with rhythmic precision, applying J/L cuts, and maintaining narrative continuity. Designing brand motion graphics in After Effects: kinetic title sequences, animated lower thirds, and animated logo stings. Executing VFX integration: planar tracking, screen replacement, and subject rotoscoping. Incorporating AI-generated footage where justified (surreal environments, macro product perspectives, or background extensions) and compositing with matched lighting, shadows, and camera grain.
subtopics: Master timeline editing: cutting live-action footage with narrative rhythm and high-retention pacing
Brand motion design: crafting custom animated typography, title cards, and logo stings in After Effects
VFX integration: executing screen replacements, object cleanup, and multi-plane 2.5D camera moves
Justified AI-generated footage integration: generating and compositing complex visual assets with matching lighting and grain
Multi-layer compositing: assembling complex visual stacks with foreground subjects, background plates, and motion graphics
Rough cut assembly: merging all visual disciplines into a cohesive 45–60 second picture-locked timeline
lessons.why_it_matters: Synthesizing editing, motion design, VFX, and AI into a singular, polished timeline is the ultimate demonstration of an industry-ready video professional.
lessons.what_learner_does: Edits the 45–60s master commercial, builds custom motion graphics, executes VFX screen replacements, and composites AI-generated environmental plates.
lessons.expected_outcome: A picture-locked 45–60 second commercial master integrating live footage, motion graphics, VFX, and justified AI assets.
lessons.example: Editing an athletic shoe commercial where live footage of a runner seamlessly transitions into an AI-generated digital terrain with glowing motion graphics.

Fairlight sound mixing: dialogue cleanup, Foley sound design, dynamic ducking, and -14 LUFS mastering
Client feedback management: translating client revision requests into actionable technical tasks
Revision simulation: executing client-requested adjustments (pacing tweaks, color trim, graphic text updates)
Delivery QA checklist: conducting exhaustive quality control for audio sync, illegal broadcast colors, and compression artifacts
Master packaging: preparing final ProRes masters, client review files, and project archival handoffs
lessons.why_it_matters: Mastery over client revisions, sound mixing, and color grading separates entry-level editors from trusted post-production supervisors.
lessons.what_learner_does: Grades the commercial in Resolve, mixes audio to -14 LUFS in Fairlight, executes simulated client revisions, and runs a comprehensive delivery QA.
lessons.expected_outcome: A broadcast-ready, fully graded, sound-mixed 45–60 second commercial master passing all delivery QA standards.

lessons.what_is_taught: The mechanics of commercial cutdowns: restructuring a 60-second master edit into an impactful 30-second version and a hyper-condensed 15-second cutdown. Preserving the core narrative hook, emotional progression, and call to action (CTA) under severe time constraints. Re-timing voiceovers, re-cutting music beds with seamless audio splices, and condensing motion graphic transitions. Maintaining story coherence and message clarity without feeling rushed or truncated.
subtopics: Master edit deconstruction: identifying non-essential beats and redundant coverage
Structuring the 30-second cut: streamlining narrative progression while retaining emotional resonance
The 15-second cutdown formula: instant hook (0-3s), problem/solution (3-10s), and punchy CTA (10-15s)
Audio re-timing: cutting music stems on bar beats and tightening voiceover spacing
Motion graphics re-scaling: accelerating lower third dwell times and animating concise logo stings
Duration quality control: ensuring exact frame-accurate runtime compliance (e.g. exactly 15;00 frames for broadcast/social)
lessons.why_it_matters: Brands allocate the majority of digital ad spend to 15s and 30s cutdowns; editors who can distill 60s stories into high-converting short formats are indispensable.

lessons.expected_outcome: Two cohesive, frame-accurate commercial cutdown edits (30s and 15s) with seamless music edits and locked CTA timing.
lessons.example: Condensing a 60-second car commercial into a 15-second high-octane cutdown focusing solely on vehicle acceleration and weekend sale pricing.

Standardizing version naming, export profiles, colour consistency, and asset packaging.

Export profiles and render optimization: configuring bitrates and NCLC color tags for flawless mobile playback
Version naming and asset packaging: building clean delivery folders (CLIENT_PROJECT_DELIVERY_V01) with master and cutdown assets

faq.question: Can complete beginners without prior editing or filmmaking experience enroll in this course?
faq.answer: Yes. Professional Video Editing is structured from foundational principles. Month 1 begins with visual storytelling grammar, shot sizes, continuity rules, and computer workspace setup before advancing into timeline mechanics. No prior experience with Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, or video theory is required.

faq.question: What is the total duration, guided hours, and weekly time commitment for this program?
faq.answer: The program spans exactly 4 Months (16 Academic Weeks) comprising 160 Guided Production Hours across 11 structured industry modules. Students should plan for 10 hours of structured guided instruction per week, plus 6 to 8 hours of independent classroom lab drills and project editing.

faq.question: How deeply is Adobe Premiere Pro covered in the curriculum?
faq.answer: Adobe Premiere Pro 26.5 serves as your primary non-linear timeline editing engine across Modules 02 and 03 (44 guided hours) plus ongoing application in Modules 07–11. You master project setup, proxy pipelines, 3-point editing, ripple/roll trimming, multicam switching, speed ramping, Essential Graphics, and export presets.

faq.question: How is DaVinci Resolve 21 taught, and what specific pages are covered?
faq.answer: DaVinci Resolve 21 receives a dedicated 24-hour deep dive in Module 05. You master the Cut and Edit pages for rapid assembly, XML conforming from Premiere, video scopes (Waveform, Vectorscope, Histogram), Log-to-Rec.709 normalization via CST nodes, Lift/Gamma/Gain primaries, 6-node tree architectures, Power Windows, qualifiers, and the Deliver page.

faq.question: Why is Adobe Photoshop included, and what lessons are taught?
faq.answer: Modern video editors are routinely required to prepare their own graphics. Module 04 dedicates 16 guided hours to Photoshop: raster resolution, Smart Objects, Levels/Curves, Camera Raw filtering, precision selection tools (Pen Tool, Select Subject, Select and Mask), and non-destructive layer hierarchies.

faq.question: What practical video graphics and thumbnail projects are created in Photoshop?
faq.answer: In Module 04, you design a complete 6-piece commercial graphic package: high-CTR YouTube thumbnails (<2MB) with bold typography and facial contrast enhancement, product advertising key visuals, transparent lower-third plates (PNG-24 with alpha), 9:16 expanded backgrounds using Generative Expand, and multi-layer PSD files imported directly into Premiere Pro.

faq.question: What Adobe After Effects skills are taught, and what are the boundaries of the motion module?
faq.answer: Module 08 provides 10 hours of editor-focused motion design: composition settings, transform keyframing, Graph Editor speed curve easing, shape layer Trim Paths, kinetic title cards, lower thirds, logo reveals, and packaging responsive MOGRT templates for Premiere Pro. The course explicitly excludes advanced VFX, 3D character rigging, multi-layer CGI, and complex expressions.

faq.question: How is audio post-production taught across Adobe Audition and DaVinci Resolve Fairlight?
faq.answer: Module 06 dedicates 16 guided hours to production audio engineering: spectral noise restoration in Adobe Audition (erasing sirens and clicks with the Healing Brush), dialogue leveling, 6-band parametric EQ, dynamics compression, and multi-track DAW mixing inside DaVinci Resolve Fairlight with submix buses and broadcast loudness normalization (-14 LUFS online / -24 LUFS broadcast).

faq.question: How is short-form vertical video editing (Reels, Shorts, TikTok) covered?
faq.answer: Module 07 teaches high-retention short-form editing: analyzing retention curves, engineering 0-to-3-second hooks, inserting pattern interrupts every 2 to 4 seconds (scale pops, punch-ins, SFX), styling dynamic word-by-word animated captions, and re-framing footage into vertical 9:16 while adhering to mobile UI safe zones.

faq.question: How is long-form YouTube editing structured in the curriculum?
faq.answer: Module 07 covers long-form YouTube editing: structuring 8-to-20 minute videos using narrative A-roll spines, B-roll contextual layering, chapter segments, lower thirds, on-screen graphic callouts, and aligning the opening 5 seconds with the Photoshop thumbnail promise to maintain high Average View Duration (AVD).

faq.question: What documentary and interview editing workflows are taught?
faq.answer: Documentary and interview editing forms the core of Project 01 and Modules 01, 02, and 06: transcribing rushes, building narrative selects, paper editing, hiding cuts with J-cuts and L-cuts, intercutting contextual B-roll to eliminate talking-head fatigue, matching multi-cam angles, and mixing dialogue to -14 LUFS.

faq.question: What specific AI-assisted editing workflows are taught in Premiere Pro and Resolve?
faq.answer: Module 09 covers practical AI workflow acceleration: Premiere Pro Speech-to-Text, Text-Based Editing, Paper Edit workflows, Auto Reframe (16:9 to 9:16), AI Enhance Speech, Generative Extend handles, and DaVinci Resolve IntelliSearch semantic media queries. All AI outputs are subjected to mandatory human verification.

faq.question: How is Adobe Firefly integrated into commercial video production?
faq.answer: Adobe Firefly and Photoshop Generative Fill/Expand are taught for commercially safe production support: expanding horizontal 16:9 frames into 9:16 vertical background plates, generating clean background plates for object removal, and generating promotional key visuals with full commercial indemnity.

faq.question: What are DaVinci Resolve 21 IntelliSearch and CineFocus, and what are their licensing limitations?
faq.answer: IntelliSearch is Resolve's AI semantic search for finding media via descriptive text, while CineFocus simulates camera depth-of-field. The course explicitly teaches students that these are Studio-edition workflow enhancements; 100% of mandatory grading and audio assessments are designed to run on the perpetual Free version of DaVinci Resolve 21.

faq.question: Are software subscriptions included, or do students need to purchase their own licenses?
faq.answer: Students provide their own software access. Adobe Creative Cloud offers discounted educational student pricing. DaVinci Resolve 21 is completely free to download and use with zero watermark. Free starter tiers and trial credits are used for Firefly and AI demonstrations.

faq.question: How do generative AI credits and platform usage limits work?
faq.answer: Generative AI compute in Firefly and Photoshop operates on standard monthly quotas. In Module 09, students are trained in prompt optimization, credit budgeting, and manual fallback workflows rather than relying on unmetered or unlimited generative compute.

faq.question: What computer hardware and GPU specifications are required for this course?
faq.answer: You need a 64-bit Windows 11 PC or macOS system (Apple Silicon M1/M2/M3/M4 or Intel Core i7) with at least 16 GB RAM (32 GB recommended for Resolve and After Effects), a dedicated GPU with minimum 4 GB VRAM (NVIDIA RTX 3060/4060 or Apple Silicon unified memory), a 512 GB internal SSD, and a fast 500 GB external SSD for media cache and 4K rushes.

faq.question: What are the three assessed portfolio projects produced during the course?
faq.answer: You build: (1) Professional Interview / Mini Documentary (2.5–3.5 min dialogue cut with Fairlight mix and Resolve grade), (2) High-Retention Short-Form Package (3 vertical 9:16 videos with hooks, animated captions, and Photoshop thumbnails), and (3) Branded Commercial Advertisement (30s commercial + 15s cutdown with speed ramps, After Effects MOGRTs, and Resolve color grade).

For the launch-batch fee of INR 29,900, 18% GST is INR 5,382, making the total payable INR 35,282. For the regular fee of INR 35,900, 18% GST is INR 6,462, making the total payable INR 42,362.

faq.question: What career and placement assistance does Nova Skills provide?

In accordance with ethical standards, Nova Skills provides verified placement assistance without making false employment or salary guarantees.

faq.question: How does this course differ from the 8-month AI-Integrated Video Editing & Motion Graphics Professional program?
faq.answer: This 4-Month (160h) program focuses on core NLE timeline editing, pacing, multicam, commercial Photoshop graphics, DaVinci Resolve color, and Fairlight audio. The 8-Month (320h) Flagship program is a comprehensive master qualification that adds deep After Effects 2D/3D kinetic animation, Mocha AE planar tracking, VFX rotoscoping/compositing, Blender 3D product integration, and frontier generative AI filmmaking (Google Flow, Runway Gen-3).

faq.question: How does this course differ from the 3-month AI Video Editing Professional course?
faq.answer: AI Video Editing Professional (3 Months, 120h) is a rapid, social-first program focused on mobile formats, lightweight AI NLE tools, and automated synthetic content. Professional Video Editing (4 Months, 160h) is an agency-grade craft program focused on dual-engine mastery (Premiere Pro + DaVinci Resolve 21), professional audio restoration, commercial Photoshop graphics, and broadcast delivery.

lessons.why_it_matters: Node trees allow surgical control over specific image elements without corrupting preceding color data, enabling rapid client revisions during commercial grading sessions.
lessons.what_learner_does: Constructs a standardized node tree, isolates an actor's face using a tracked Power Window and HSL Qualifier, corrects skin tones to the vectorscope line, and darkens the background.
lessons.expected_outcome: A multi-node graded sequence with isolated, protected skin tones and tracked secondary adjustments.
lessons.example: Using a tracked circular Power Window on an interviewee to boost face luminance by +0.5 stops while slightly desaturating a bright red exit sign in the background.

lessons.what_is_taught: Audio fundamentals (sample rates, bit depths, mono vs stereo, gain staging), peak meters, clipping thresholds, dialogue editing, trimming breaths, applying micro-crossfades, and capturing continuous room tone.
subtopics: Configuring 48 kHz / 24-bit audio timelines and understanding headroom
Input gain staging vs timeline track volume faders
Dialogue trimming: removing false starts, stuttering, and excessively loud breaths
Applying 10ms Constant Power crossfades across all edit points to prevent clicks
Looping room tone under dialogue gaps to maintain atmospheric continuity
lessons.why_it_matters: Clean dialogue editing is the bedrock of good audio. Inconsistent room tone and clicking edit points destroy listener trust faster than imperfect video.
lessons.what_learner_does: Takes raw interview dialogue, normalizes gain to -6dB, trims distracting breaths, applies micro-crossfades, and builds a seamless room tone bed.
lessons.expected_outcome: A seamless, click-free dialogue track with natural breathing rhythms and consistent room tone.
lessons.example: Inserting a 2-second looped room tone room bed underneath a pause in conversation to bridge two disparate takes without an acoustic drop-out.

lessons.lesson_title: Production Equalization, Dynamics Compression & Dialogue Clarity

subtopics: Applying an 80 Hz high-pass filter to eliminate microphone handling rumble and AC hum
Sweeping a high-Q notch filter to find and eliminate ringing room resonance frequencies
Setting up dialogue compression (3:1 ratio, 20ms attack, 100ms release) to smooth vocal volume
De-essing harsh frequencies between 5 kHz and 8 kHz to prevent piercing sibilance
Setting a hard limiter ceiling at -1.0 dBFS to prevent digital clipping distortion
lessons.why_it_matters: Raw recorded voices vary wildly in volume; proper EQ and compression make dialogue sound rich, polished, and effortlessly understandable on any speaker.
lessons.what_learner_does: Processes raw dialogue using parametric EQ, applies multiband compression, tames harsh sibilance, and limits master peaks.
lessons.expected_outcome: A broadcast-grade dialogue track with warm presence, consistent dynamic range, and zero distortion.
lessons.example: Boosting 3.5 kHz with a gentle bell curve to bring an actor's vocal articulation to the front of a dense mix.

subtopics: Building layered sonic worlds: pairing ambient backgrounds with specific Foley actions
Designing transition sound effects (risers, whooshes, sub drops) to sell visual cuts
Editing music tracks: cutting on the beat, looping sections, and timing dramatic endings
Adobe Audition Spectral Frequency Display: isolating unwanted acoustic events visually
Using Audition's Healing Brush to surgically erase a police siren from an outdoor interview
lessons.why_it_matters: Sound design creates 50% of the emotional impact of a video, while spectral audio repair rescues irreplaceable dialogue that cannot be re-recorded.
lessons.what_learner_does: Rescues an interview ruined by background siren noise in Audition, layers Foley and ambient sound effects for a commercial scene, and cuts music to match edit pacing.
lessons.expected_outcome: A rich multi-track soundscape and a restored dialogue track stripped of background sirens.
lessons.example: Surgically painting over a telephone ring in Audition's spectral display without muffling the speaker's overlapping voice.

lessons.what_learner_does: Mixes a commercial video in Fairlight, configures submix buses, applies auto-ducking, audits AI voice isolation, normalizes master audio to -14 LUFS, and exports DME stems.

Deliver compliant master exports tailored for YouTube, Instagram Reels, TikTok, corporate communications, and broadcast with caption-safe and title-safe area compliance.
Execute rigorous frame-by-frame Quality Control (QC) audits: detecting black frames, audio clipping above -1.0 dBFS, missing media, caption typos, color gamut mismatches, and lip-sync errors.
Manage professional client review workflows: setting up timecoded review links (Frame.io), interpreting subjective feedback, tracking revisions (v01 to Locked), and managing client deadlines.

Perform full media management and project archiving: consolidating media via Premiere Project Manager and Resolve Archives (.dra), relinking assets, organizing font/music licenses, and compiling client handoff packages.
what_you_will_learn: Mastering and export: codecs, containers, H.264/H.265, bitrates, resolutions, frame rates, aspect ratios, and alpha channels.
Platform delivery: YouTube exports, Instagram Reels, Shorts, social advertising, corporate video, safe areas, SDR/HDR, and mobile layouts.
Quality control: black frames, audio clipping, missing media, caption errors, color mismatch, frame glitches, crop problems, and sync.
Client workflow: review links, approval processes, client notes, revision tracking, version naming, and deadline management.
Media management: project archiving, consolidation, relinking, source file packaging, font/music licensing, and backup.

subtopics: Codecs: lossy delivery compression (H.264, H.265/HEVC, AV1) vs visually lossless editing codecs (Apple ProRes 422/HQ, Avid DNxHR)
Containers: wrapper formats (.mp4, .mov, .mxf) and their audio/video/metadata compatibility
H.264 and H.265 compression: profile levels (Main vs High), hardware accelerated encoding, and 10-bit HEVC
Bitrates: calculating data rates, target vs maximum bitrates, Constant Bitrate (CBR) vs Variable Bitrate (VBR 1-pass and 2-pass)
Resolution standards: Full HD (1920x1080), 2K, 4K UHD (3840x2160), and DCI 4K (4096x2160)
Frame rates and timebase conform: maintaining strict delivery frame rates without accidental pulldown or frame blending
Aspect ratios: 16:9 widescreen, 9:16 mobile vertical, 1:1 square, and 4:5 social feeds
Color space awareness: Rec.709 display color, Gamma 2.4 vs Gamma 2.2, and embedding Rec.709-A tags to prevent QuickTime wash-out
Audio delivery: uncompressed LPCM 48 kHz / 24-bit stereo vs AAC 320 kbps compressed delivery
Alpha channel concepts: QuickTime ProRes 4444 (32-bit RGB + Alpha) for motion graphic overlay exports
YouTube exports: optimizing bitrates (12-16 Mbps for 1080p, 45-60 Mbps for 4K) to avoid heavy YouTube re-compression
Instagram Reels: encoding parameters (1080x1920 at 30fps/60fps, 10-15 Mbps H.264) for artifact-free mobile upload
YouTube Shorts: high-velocity loop encoding, instant hook rendering, and audio master leveling
Social advertising: technical specifications for Meta Ads Manager, Google Ads, and TikTok Ads Manager
Corporate video: intranet hosting requirements, email-friendly lightweight preview cuts, and high-res presentation masters
Caption-safe and title-safe areas: 80% title-safe and 90% action-safe boundaries
SDR and HDR fundamentals: Standard Dynamic Range (SDR) Rec.709 delivery vs High Dynamic Range (HDR10 / HLG) awareness
Mobile-safe layouts: avoiding TikTok/Reels UI buttons, caption text overlays, and top/bottom profile interface chrome
Black frames and flash frames: scanning cuts to detect accidental single-frame black gaps or leftover split frames

target_audience.best_for: Beginners with basic computer literacy, content creators, video editors, designers, marketing creatives and aspiring AI video producers seeking professional mastery of generative video production pipelines.
target_audience.not_for: Individuals seeking purely theoretical AI overviews without hands-on video editing, or those looking for automated one-click video generators without professional post-production craft.
target_audience.who_should_take_foundation_first: Candidates lacking basic personal computer operation, file management, or basic internet research skills should complete foundational digital literacy prior to enrollment.

required: Basic computer literacy (operating system navigation, file management, and web browsing)
Creative problem-solving mindset and passion for visual storytelling and commercial video
Commitment of 8–10 hours per week for guided studio sessions, practical labs, and portfolio development
recommended: Familiarity with digital media formats, social video platforms (YouTube, Instagram, TikTok), and basic creative tools
Basic exposure to photo or video editing concepts is helpful but not mandatory

system_requirements.os: Windows 10/11 (64-bit) or macOS Monterey 12.0 or newer
system_requirements.processor: Multi-core Intel Core i5/i7/i9, AMD Ryzen 5/7/9, or Apple Silicon (M1/M2/M3/M4)
system_requirements.ram: 16 GB RAM minimum (32 GB recommended for seamless After Effects compositing and 4K playback)
system_requirements.gpu: Dedicated GPU with 4GB+ VRAM (NVIDIA RTX series recommended for AI feature acceleration) or Apple Silicon Unified Memory
system_requirements.storage: 250 GB+ available high-speed SSD storage for project media caches, scratch disks, and assets
system_requirements.internet: Reliable high-speed broadband connection (50+ Mbps recommended) for cloud AI generation and high-definition video streaming

not_required: Prior professional video editing experience or film school degree is not required
Advanced programming, Python coding, or local model fine-tuning knowledge is not required

overview.positioning: Create Cinematic AI Commercials. Master the Complete Production Workflow. Learn to conceptualize, direct, generate, edit and deliver professional AI-powered videos using Adobe Firefly, Google Flow, Kling AI, Runway, Premiere Pro, After Effects and professional post-production workflows.
overview.short_description: Create Cinematic AI Commercials. Master the Complete Production Workflow. Learn to conceptualize, direct, generate, edit and deliver professional AI-powered videos using Adobe Firefly, Google Flow, Kling AI, Runway, Premiere Pro, After Effects and professional post-production workflows.
overview.full_description: An intensive 5-month professional specialization program designed for content creators, video editors, designers, marketing creatives, and aspiring AI video producers. hands_on_tech.overview: October 2026 commercial generative AI video production toolchain. Seamlessly bridges cutting-edge multi-model AI video generation (Adobe Firefly Video, Google Flow / Veo 2 & 3, Kling AI v1.5/v2, Runway Gen-3 Alpha / Turbo) with enterprise non-linear timeline editing in Adobe Premiere Pro 2026, hybrid compositing and planar tracking in Adobe After Effects 2026, high-fidelity reference frame engineering in Adobe Photoshop, studio voice synthesis in ElevenLabs, Hollywood node-based color grading in DaVinci Resolve 21, and broadcast 4K upscaling in Topaz Video AI.

software_licensing_and_zero_cost_policy.credit_budget_and_anti_burn_protocol: Cloud generative compute is metered across platforms. To protect student resources, the program enforces a mandatory 3-Tier Draft-to-Hero protocol: Tier 1 ideation and prompt testing in Claude/ChatGPT and Midjourney Relaxed mode; Tier 2 motion blocking in fast/turbo modes (Runway Gen-3 Turbo / Kling Standard); Tier 3 single-pass hero renders in full-credit engines. Zero promises of unlimited credits are made.
software_licensing_and_zero_cost_policy.ethical_likeness_and_voice_rights_govern: Strict prohibition against synthesizing real-person celebrity likenesses, public figures, or cloning human voices without verifiable, written commercial consent. All character workflows leverage synthetic personas, customized turnaround sheets, or authorized digital ambassadors.
software_licensing_and_zero_cost_policy.commercial_safety_and_indemnification: Delineates enterprise-grade, legally indemnified models (Adobe Firefly Video, trained on licensed Adobe Stock) from research-oriented open or semi-closed models. Students learn C2PA Content Credentials, watermark mitigation, and commercial release documentation.
software_licensing_and_zero_cost_policy.zero_cost_local_production_stack: DaVinci Resolve 21 Free edition is utilized for Hollywood-grade color grading and Fairlight audio post, providing full node trees, scopes, and -14 LUFS loudness mastering at zero software cost. Creative Cloud tools run on standard student licenses without unreleased experimental beta dependencies.

faq.question: Who can join the Generative AI Video Production Professional program?
faq.answer: This course is open to beginners with basic computer literacy, content creators, video editors, graphic designers, marketing creatives, and aspiring video producers seeking professional mastery of generative video pipelines. No prior filmmaking degree or coding knowledge is required.

faq.question: Is previous video editing required before enrolling?
faq.answer: No. Previous video editing experience is not required. The program is structured progressively. Month 1 builds foundational visual storytelling grammar, shot sizes, framing, and scriptwriting before introducing hands-on editing in Premiere Pro (Month 3) and After Effects (Month 4). However, students with basic computer navigation skills will advance most rapidly.

faq.question: What does 'AI-first commercial video training' mean?
faq.answer: It means generative AI tools are not taught as isolated gimmicks, but as core production engines integrated directly into an industry-standard post-production workflow. You learn to direct AI models to generate shots based on real commercial scripts, and then edit, composite, grade, and finish those shots in Premiere Pro, After Effects, and DaVinci Resolve.

faq.question: Why is the program structured across 5 months and 200 guided hours?
faq.answer: Mastering commercial AI video requires both generative proficiency and professional post-production craft. Across 200 guided hours (40 hours per month), students master pre-production (Mo. 1), video generation and consistency (Mo. 2), Premiere Pro editing (Mo. 3), After Effects compositing and audio (Mo. 4), and commercial campaigns with capstone portfolio production (Mo. 5).

faq.question: Which generative AI video models are taught in the course?
faq.answer: The program provides deep hands-on training across Adobe Firefly Video, Google Flow (utilizing supported Veo video models), Kling AI (v1.5/v2), and Runway (Gen-2 / Gen-3 Alpha). Students learn model selection based on cost, control, camera physics, and rendering quality.

faq.question: How is Adobe Firefly integrated into the commercial workflow?
faq.answer: Adobe Firefly is used for commercially safe text-to-image and text-to-video generation, reference-guided frame expansion, Firefly Boards pre-visualization, and direct integration with Adobe Photoshop and Premiere Pro Generative Extend.

faq.question: How are Google Flow and supported Veo models utilized?
faq.answer: Google Flow and supported Veo video models are used for high-fidelity cinematic camera motions, text-to-video scene generation, start/end-frame interpolation, and multi-shot visual planning with cinematic depth.

faq.question: What role does Kling AI play in the production pipeline?
faq.answer: Kling AI is deployed for complex subject motion, photorealistic human movement, start-frame to end-frame camera transitions, and controlled image-to-video generation requiring high temporal consistency.

faq.question: How is Runway (Gen-2 / Gen-3 Alpha) deployed?
faq.answer: Runway Gen-3 Alpha is utilized for high-speed dynamic camera movements, camera control brushes, text-to-video, image-to-video, and generating atmospheric environment plates for VFX compositing.

faq.question: Why is Adobe Photoshop included in a video production course?
faq.answer: Photoshop is essential for visual asset development in Month 1 and Module 04: generating clean reference plates, removing AI generation artifacts, fixing anatomical anomalies, masking clean product plates, and creating graphic title overlays for video editing.

faq.question: Why is Adobe Premiere Pro the primary editorial backbone?
faq.answer: Generative video clips are meaningless without precise editorial storytelling. Premiere Pro (Module 07 & 08) provides classical 3-point timeline assembly, trim mechanics, J/L cut pacing, Text-Based Editing, Auto Reframe, and Enhance Speech audio cleanup.

faq.question: How is Adobe After Effects used for hybrid compositing and motion design?
faq.answer: In Module 09, After Effects is used to composite synthetic AI environment plates with filmed live-action talent, perform Mocha AE planar screen tracking on mobile devices, extract moving subjects with Roto Brush 3, and animate commercial kinetic typography.

faq.question: How does ElevenLabs power the commercial audio workflow?
faq.answer: ElevenLabs is taught in Module 10 for professional commercial voiceover engineering: script pacing, stability/clarity tuning, emotional inflection, SSML phonetic controls, multilingual voice cloning, and authorized voice-consent documentation.

faq.question: Why is DaVinci Resolve 21 taught for color grading?
faq.answer: Disparate AI video engines output mismatched color temperatures, contrast curves, and black levels. DaVinci Resolve 21 Color page is used to balance exposures via video scopes (Waveform, Vectorscope), lock skin tones, and apply unified cinematic film LUTs.

faq.question: When and how is Topaz Video AI deployed?
faq.answer: Topaz Video AI is deployed in Module 10 for neural video enhancement: upscaling 720p/1080p AI clips to crisp 4K, removing synthetic noise and compression artifacts with the Proteus model, restoring facial detail via the Iris model, and interpolating 24fps video to smooth 60fps with Chronos.

faq.question: How does the curriculum solve character and product consistency across shots?
faq.answer: Module 06 teaches systematic character and product consistency: locked turnaround reference sheets, seed parameters, style reference matching (`--sref` / image prompts), clean-plate masking in Photoshop, and start/end-frame anchor workflows.

faq.question: How do start-frame and end-frame animation workflows work?
faq.answer: In supported engines like Kling AI and Runway, students generate a specific start keyframe and end keyframe, directing the AI model to compute the in-between camera motion and subject transformations accurately without hallucinating unpredictable endings.

faq.question: How are real filmed footage and AI-generated elements composited together?
faq.answer: Module 09 and Project 04 teach hybrid plate compositing: extracting filmed actors using green screen or Roto Brush 3, matching camera perspective and horizon lines to AI environment plates, adding artificial contact shadows, equalizing camera sensor grain, and applying edge light wraps.

faq.question: What are the five mandatory portfolio projects?
faq.answer: Students complete 5 assessed projects: P1: AI Commercial Pre-production Kit (treatment deck & script); P2: Cinematic AI Product Teaser (15s luxury product reveal); P3: Performance-Ready Social Media Video (9:16 vertical ad with A/B hooks); P4: Hybrid AI + Live-Action Commercial Shot (VFX composite); and P5: Final AI Commercial Advertising Campaign (12-asset capstone suite) plus a 60–90-second showreel.

faq.question: What is the Final Commercial Advertising Campaign capstone project?
faq.answer: The capstone (Module 13) is a comprehensive commercial campaign for an enterprise brief containing a 30s master commercial, 15s cutdown, 6s bumper, 2 alternative opening hooks, 9:16 and 16:9 exports, storyboard, editable project files, prompt logs, consent evidence, and a signed technical QC report.

faq.question: Are AI tool subscriptions, compute credits, or commercial assets provided by the institute?
faq.answer: No. Nova Skills maintains complete commercial transparency: students utilize student-managed free trial tiers, educational allowances, or purchase personal credits according to their project generation needs. Nova Skills does not claim institute-managed unlimited credits, paid premium subscriptions, or commercial stock libraries are bundled without verified provisioning.

faq.question: What are the minimum hardware and computer requirements?
faq.answer: A modern 64-bit Windows 10/11 or macOS computer with a multi-core processor (Intel i5/i7/i9, AMD Ryzen, or Apple Silicon M-series), 16GB RAM minimum (32GB recommended), dedicated GPU with 4GB+ VRAM (NVIDIA RTX recommended for AI features), 250GB+ SSD storage, and 50+ Mbps high-speed internet.

faq.question: What are the legal rules for voice and likeness permissions in synthetic media?
faq.answer: Module 12 enforces strict legal governance: cloning living individuals without signed talent release contracts is prohibited. Students learn to draft voice and likeness consent releases, comply with publicity rights, and maintain ethical synthetic media authorizations.

faq.question: What are the commercial rights and copyright boundaries for AI-generated video?
faq.answer: Module 12 covers commercial licensing tiers across all tools, public domain vs copyrighted training data, human authorship thresholds required for copyright registration, and avoidance of proprietary brand trademarks.

faq.question: What is the regular fee and introductory launch batch pricing?
faq.answer: The regular program fee is ₹39,900 + applicable statutory 18% GST. For the introductory launch cohort, the tuition is ₹34,900 + applicable statutory 18% GST. Nova Skills maintains a transparent pricing policy with zero fabricated discounts.

faq.question: Are installment payment options (EMI) available?
faq.answer: Flexible installment options (EMI) are available exclusively through approved institutional financial partners, subject to individual credit verification and partner terms.

faq.question: What career preparation and portfolio support does Nova Skills provide?
faq.answer: Students receive 1-on-1 portfolio reviews, showreel pacing critiques, LinkedIn/Behance optimization guidance, and mock client pitch simulations. In accordance with ethical standards, Nova Skills does not offer guaranteed job placements, fixed salary promises, or senior management appointments.

faq.question: What is the difference between this course, Professional Video Editing (4 Months), and the 8-Month Flagship?
faq.answer: The core difference lies in technical orientation: Professional Video Editing (4 Months / 160h) focuses primarily on classical non-linear editing, multicam, Photoshop graphics, and DaVinci color grading for filmed footage. Generative AI Video Production Professional (5 Months / 200h) is an AI-first commercial specialization focusing on generative models (Firefly, Veo, Kling, Runway), synthetic consistency, and hybrid VFX. The 8-Month Flagship is a comprehensive diploma covering both classical editing, full 3D motion design, and advanced broadcast pipelines.

modules.module_purpose: Translate 2D CAD plans into precise 3D architectural geometry.

lessons.what_learner_does: Models the exterior walls and roof of a modern house.
lessons.expected_outcome: Completed primary exterior structure.

lessons.what_learner_does: Models and places windows, doors, and mullions.
lessons.expected_outcome: Fully detailed exterior envelope.

lessons.what_learner_does: Models a custom staircase and kitchen island.
lessons.expected_outcome: Complete structural model ready for texturing.

modules.business_application: Rapid prototyping of architectural designs for client approval.
modules.expected_outcome: Accurate 3D whitebox model of the residential project.

modules.module_purpose: Apply realistic surfaces to architectural models using V-Ray materials.
what_you_will_learn: Understand the Principles of Physically Based Rendering (PBR).
Create complex V-Ray materials like glass, metal, and concrete.
Use UVW mapping for correct texture alignment.

lessons.what_learner_does: Creates architectural glazing and brushed aluminum materials.
lessons.expected_outcome: Realistic windows and metallic fixtures in the scene.

lessons.what_learner_does: Lights the villa exterior for a midday shot.

modules.expected_outcome: Mastery of V-Ray illumination techniques.

what_you_will_learn: Optimize V-Ray render settings for quality and speed.

lessons.what_learner_does: Configures optimal settings and renders the final 4K images.

lessons.expected_outcome: Client-ready, photorealistic architectural visualization.

best_practices: Address the client by name whenever it can be discovered from past job review histories.

faq.question: Does proposal writing matter if my portfolio is already strong?
faq.answer: Yes. Most clients receive 30+ bids and will never open your portfolio link unless your proposal hook convinces them you understand their exact problem.

faq.question: Can I use ChatGPT to write my proposals?
faq.answer: We teach you how to use AI for researching client technical stacks and drafting outlines, but show why raw AI copy-paste leads to instant disqualification by savvy clients.

faq.question: How fast will this improve my response rate?
faq.answer: Students typically see immediate improvements in client message responses within their first 5 to 10 tailored submissions using the diagnostic framework.

faq.question: How much revenue should I be making before starting this course?
faq.answer: We recommend earning at least $2,000/month consistently as a solo freelancer so you have proven skills and existing clients to transition into your agency model.

faq.question: Do I need to hire full-time staff immediately?
faq.answer: No. The entire modern agency framework is built around agile, on-demand specialist contractors, keeping your overhead near zero while maintaining high profit margins.

faq.question: What tools are needed to run an agency?
faq.answer: You will learn to master ClickUp, Notion, Slack, Loom, and Stripe. Most of these can be started on free or low-cost tiers.

modules.module_purpose: Understand and manage the physical and mental symptoms of anxiety.

lessons.what_learner_does: Read a text using extreme variations in voice, then find a natural balance.

best_practices: Red wire is for Power (5V), Black wire is for Ground (GND).

best_practices: Design the thumbnail and write the title before filming the video.

faq.question: Do I need expensive camera gear?
faq.answer: No. A modern smartphone and a good cheap microphone are enough to start. Content and audio matter more than 4K video.

faq.answer: We touch on Shorts as a growth tool, but the primary focus is on long-form content.

certification.title: Certified Tally & GST Professional

faq.question: Do I need an accounting background?
faq.answer: Basic knowledge of debits and credits is highly recommended to grasp the concepts quickly.

faq.question: Is Tally Prime different from Tally ERP 9?
faq.answer: Yes, Tally Prime has a modernized interface and improved navigation, which we cover extensively.

faq.question: Will we learn actual GST portal filing?
faq.answer: We simulate the process and show how to generate the JSON files required for the actual portal.
